api.title: REST API
api.subtitle: Integrate Datia into your platform via our REST API
api.description: The Datia REST API lets you create products, add certified states, and query your organization's data programmatically. You can integrate it into your own applications using an authentication token.

capabilities.title: What can you do with the API?

createProducts.title: Create products
createProducts.description: Register new products in the system by specifying their identifier, name, and description.

addStates.title: Add states
addStates.description: Attach certified states to products using the status types configured in your organization.

queryData.title: Query data
queryData.description: List and filter products with cursor pagination, search by name or category.

tokenAuth.title: Token authentication
tokenAuth.description: Each call is authenticated with a Bearer API token associated with your organization.

sandbox.title: Testing environment (Sandbox)
sandbox.description: The interactive documentation includes a pre-configured sandbox environment. You can make real API calls without data persisting in the production database: everything is stored temporarily on the server and discarded.

noRealData.title: No real data
noRealData.description: Products and states you create in the sandbox do not appear in your dashboard.

ephemeral.title: Ephemeral environment
ephemeral.description: Sandbox data is automatically discarded when the server restarts.

noDb.title: No database impact
noDb.description: No sandbox call writes to the production database.

realStatusTypes.title: Real status types
realStatusTypes.description: The sandbox reads the status types you have configured in your organization so tests are representative.

howTo.title: How to open the testing environment
howTo.step1: Click Open testing environment to access the interactive documentation.
howTo.step2: When it opens, the sandbox token is already pre-configured in the authentication panel — you don't need to create or paste any token.
howTo.step3: Select the Sandbox server in the documentation selector to point to /api/v1-sandbox — or use that URL directly from your own tools.
howTo.step4: Run endpoints directly from the browser. Any data you create is temporary and does not affect production.
